incident-bot: Pager: hosted-api - queue depth spiked to 18,400, p95=6.8s p99=22.3s, timeouts rising. Alerting SRE oncall.
emma (oncall): taking this. hitting the incident runbook now. tagging @kai and @sara.
kai (sre): I see the autoscaler failing to provision new GPU nodes — provisioner API returning 429 / QuotaExceeded errors starting ~10:12 UTC. digging into logs.
sara (eng-runtime): any indication this is due to a recent rollout? configs look unchanged. models in prod are same versions.
mike (infra): cloud control plane shows "Requested GPUs: 64, Available: 0" for the region us-west2. customer demand spike looks like a sudden RTU from a large tenant. I'm opening a quota request but that won't be instant.
jordan (prodops): can we shift traffic to dedicated pools or fall back to smaller model variants? need quick mitigation to avoid p99s blowing further.
kai (sre): autoscaler log excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T10:12:58Z INFO autoscaler.provisioner.request id=abc123 status=429 body="QuotaExceeded: Requested 8 GPUs, available 0"
2026-03-15T10:13:12Z WARN autoscaler.backoff id=abc123 retry=1
2026-03-15T10:13:40Z ERROR autoscaler.giveup id=abc123 reason="quota exhausted, aborting provisioning"
```
kai (sre): autoscaler retries are exponential with a short cap; once quota responses start, it stops creating new capacity. that's the main failure mode here.
emma (oncall): immediate mitigations?
sara (eng-runtime): enable fallback routing to CPU-backed smaller model for non-critical traffic. we have a routing flag per tenant. I'll push a temporary increase.
mike (infra): starting a manual dedicated pool (urgent-dedicated-1) using our reserved account to absorb some traffic. won't be instant, ~6-8 minutes to warm up.
jordan (prodops): also toggling aggressive queue shedding for low-priority requests: set queued_request_ttl=10s for best-effort. that will reduce p99 for high-priority flows.
emma (oncall): commands you used? paste for audit.
sara (eng-runtime): command to update routing (internal):
```
# route 30% of hosted traffic to cpu-fallback model
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  https://internal.redwood/api/v1/routing/hosted -d '{"fallback_percent":30}'
```
jordan (prodops): queue shedding toggle:
```
POST /configs/queues/hosted -d '{"queued_request_ttl":10, "priority_policy":"preserve_sla"}'
```
mike (infra): provisioner manual spot-pool command (internal):
```
provisioner create-pool --name urgent-dedicated-1 --gpus 16 --flavor a100 --region us-west2
```
mike (infra): started pool creation at 10:14 UTC, logs show instance launches in progress.
kai (sre): routing change + shedding helped — p95 dropped from 6.8s -> 3.1s within 90s, p99 improving but still elevated (now ~11s). queue depth down to 7.2k.
emma (oncall): customer impact? who to notify?
jordan (prodops): initial impact assessment: no full outages, but several high-volume customers see increased client-side timeouts; internal error rate for best-effort tier jumped to 4.1% in last 10m. emailing top-5 affected customers now.
sara (eng-runtime): interesting note: autoscaler has a config flag allow_quota_fallback=false which prevents provisioning on accounts that would exceed quota; given there was cross-tenant quota pressure, autoscaler opted not to create small fallback nodes. we should consider temporary override in this case.
kai (sre): we patched autoscaler to allow a controlled fallback (limit 8 GPUs per attempt) — patch applied 10:18 UTC to dev branch and hotfixed to oncall.
mike (infra): manual pool is up and accepting traffic at 10:20 UTC. routing now sends ~22% to the new pool.
kai (sre): metrics now: queue depth 2.0k, p95=2.3s, p99=7.1s, timeouts dropping. still monitoring for second wave.
emma (oncall): good. next: open ticket with cloud to raise regional GPU quota; include spike evidence. @mike please attach autoscaler logs.
mike (infra): ticket created with cloud support (CS-10877) at 10:23 UTC, quoting sample logs and peak utilization.
jordan (prodops): follow-up items: 1) evaluate autoscaler quota-fallback policy, 2) add rate-limit guardrail for new tenants to prevent single tenant RTU, 3) runbook update to include manual pool steps. putting tasks in incident board.
sara (eng-runtime): runbook note: add a quick toggle to permit "fallthrough-provisioning" for short windows. we'll draft a safe plan.
emma (oncall): handoff: I'm staying on for 30 more minutes to stabilize, then handing to @maria (night). leaving summary below.
emma (oncall): HANDOFF SUMMARY -> 10:30 UTC
- Cause: sudden spike from single tenant + regional GPU quota exhaustion -> autoscaler received QuotaExceeded and stopped provisioning.
- Mitigations applied: fallback routing to CPU model (30%), queue shedding TTL=10s for best-effort, manual dedicated pool urgent-dedicated-1 (16 GPUs) created, autoscaler patch to allow controlled fallback provisioning.
- Impact: elevated p99/timeouts for ~12 minutes; best-effort tier error rate peaked at 4.1%; no full customer outages. Top-5 customers notified.
- Open actions: cloud quota request CS-10877, runbook change PR, evaluate rate-limits per tenant, monitor for reoccurrence.
emma (oncall): @maria - please take the rest of the on-call, watch stock p99 and queue depth for next 2 hours. escalate to infra/eng if p99 > 10s for more than 5m.
maria (oncall-night): taking over. thanks for the handoff. I'll keep the channel updated and coordinate with @mike and @kai.
incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated, monitoring. severity: sev3 -> under observation.
emma (oncall): closing this thread once stable and after post-incident writeup. thanks all :heart:
